nodes.title: Note: Usage
widgets_values:
## Full-reference scoring (target vs reference)

`Load Image` (top) runs through `Add Noise to Image` to become the **target** - a
deliberately distorted copy, so the numbers have something to measure - and the
second `Load Image` is the **reference**, the clean original. Two full-reference
metrics score that pair:

- **pyiqa FR Score** with LPIPS+ (VGG, semantic weighting): **lower is better**,
  0-1.
- **FGResQ FR Score** with the FGResQ FR pair variant: **higher is better**. It
  returns five values per pair; the preview here shows the 4th, `verdict` - the
  rank in words (`target_better` / `reference_better` / `similar`).

`Preview Image` in the middle shows the noisy target, so you can see what is being
judged. A single image pair is scored at a time here; both score nodes accept a
batch, so you can feed several pairs at once and get one result per pair.

## How to run

1. Point both `Load Image` nodes at your own images: the reference is the image you
   trust, the target is the one you are judging. If you already have a
   produced/restored image, bypass `Add Noise to Image` and wire it straight into
   both score nodes.
2. Queue the prompt.
3. Read the two `Preview as Text` widgets: the FR score and the FGResQ verdict.

The first run downloads weights (FGResQ's are the big ones, ~1.2 GB for its two
files) into `ComfyUI/models/pyiqa/`.

## Order matters

The **target** wire is the image being judged; the **reference** wire is the
pristine original. Swapping them flips the FGResQ verdict, and the two per-image
scores swap with it. Target and reference must have the same batch size - one
image each here.

Both score nodes use `memory_management = unload model (VRAM + RAM)`, so each
metric frees its weights right after scoring. Use `keep loaded` when scoring many
pairs in a row.
